source_caption:
For the movie’s explosive climax, David Fincher pushed Andrew Garfield to his absolute emotional breaking point. Fincher, known for his relentless demand for multiple takes, made Garfield perform the physically and emotionally draining confrontation around 40 times. Garfield threw himself so entirely into the betrayal that his anger began to feel incredibly real on set. Jesse Eisenberg later admitted in interviews that he was genuinely terrified while sitting at the desk, because Garfield’s rage was so palpable and unhinged during those takes. By the end of the grueling shoot, Garfield was completely exhausted, having left every ounce of energy he had on the floor. In a rare break from his usually stoic demeanor, Fincher actually pulled Garfield aside afterward just to tell him how proud he was of the performance.

The Social Network (2010), directed by David Fincher, starring Jesse Eisenberg, Andrew Garfield, Justin Timberlake. A brilliant but socially inept Harvard undergraduate builds a revolutionary social networking platform in his dorm room, only to face devastating, multi-million dollar lawsuits from the twin brothers who claim he stole their idea and the loyal best friend who helped him fund it.

source_details.synopsis: The Social Network is a 2010 American biographical drama film directed by David Fincher and written by Aaron Sorkin. Based on the 2009 book The Accidental Billionaires by Ben Mezrich, the film portrays the founding of the social networking website Facebook. It stars Jesse Eisenberg as Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg, with Andrew Garfield as co-founder Eduardo Saverin, Justin Timberlake as Sean Parker, Armie Hammer as Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, and Max Minghella as Divya Narendra. Neither Zuckerberg nor any other Facebook staff were involved with the project, although Saverin was a consultant for Mezrich's book. Production began when Sorkin signed on to write the screenplay.
